title: Shared bpm_test's tenant_default schema was fully dropped and reprovisioned mid-lineage (2026-08-08 08:19:53 UTC), silently recreating 18+ GLOBAL_REGISTRY shadow tables that GBL-134/GBL-136 had already dropped
registered_by: ISSUE-FIXER (WF03-GH573-20260808, incidental finding while validating the ISS-0620/GH-573 forward-fix)
related_to: ISS-0620 / GH #573 -- the run during which this was discovered

GH #533 -- a related but distinct prior incident (destructive tenant_default DROP SCHEMA recovery fallback in a test file, already fixed) that establishes tenant_default reprovisioning as a recurring risk in this shared database
scope: Shared bpm_test database only (localhost:5453/bpm_test). workspace r-co-2's bpm_dev database is confirmed clean (0 duplicates) -- this is isolated to the shared test database.
symptom: python3 tools/lint_dual_schema_table_names.py (BLOCKER exit 1) reports 18 table names duplicated between public and tenant_default in bpm_test: agent_bootstrap_audit, agent_bootstrap_state, agent_identity_binding, agent_secret_rotation, federation_attribute_mapping, group_roles, idp_adapter_audit, idp_federation_binding, idp_operation_ledger, idp_transaction_log, instance_definition_snapshots, role_permissions, sessions, sla_records, subsystem_health_probe, tenant_artifact_activations, user_groups, webhook_deliveries. All 18 were already dropped once by GBL-134 (applied 2026-08-08 05:44:11 UTC) or GBL-135/GBL-136, yet are present again. Confirmed via schema_migrations: tenant_default's entire migration ledger in bpm_test was re-applied from scratch in a ~2.5 second burst at 2026-08-08 08:19:53.236205 to 08:19:55.782928 UTC (75 rows, 001_event_store.sql through 1137_iss0156_entity_instance_projection_backfill.sql) -- well AFTER GBL-134 (05:44:11), GBL-135 (05:44:16), and GBL-136 (07:15:57) all ran. The only explanation consistent with the evidence is that tenant_default was dropped (as a schema) and fully reprovisioned by something running against the shared bpm_test container between 07:15:57 and 08:19:53 UTC.
root_cause_analysis: Not fully diagnosed -- filed as an incidental discovery, not this run's task. Two candidate mechanisms, neither confirmed: (1) a stale zig build migrate/test-integration binary compiled from a checkout that predates commit a2a8c68 (which added GBL-134/135/136 and the -- scope: public header to migration 094) running against the shared bpm_test container from a sibling workspace (this repo's parallel-workspaces setup has at least one other checkout, r-co, sharing the same host); such a binary would not know to skip the newly-scoped public-only migrations during a tenant_default provisioning pass, explaining why even 094_entity_subsystem.sql (which now carries -- scope: public, confirmed present at byte offset 987 of the file, well inside migrationScope()'s 4096-byte read window) was replayed into tenant_default at 08:19:55. (2) A test cleanup/reset path similar to the one already fixed in GH #533 (test_api08_auth.zig's destructive tenant_default DROP SCHEMA recovery) recurring via a different, not-yet-identified call site. Both are plausible; distinguishing them requires further investigation this run did not perform (out of scope -- discovered while validating an unrelated forward-fix migration).
impact: python3 tools/lint_dual_schema_table_names.py is a BLOCKER gate (per CLAUDE.md CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR / lint conventions) and currently fails against the shared bpm_test database with 18 findings that are not fixable by re-running GBL-134/135/136 (idempotent DROP TABLE IF EXISTS-style guards mean they will simply no-op against tables that were dropped once and came back via a different path). Any pipeline step that runs this linter against bpm_test will see a false-BLOCKER-looking failure that is actually a stale/reprovisioned-schema artifact, not a new migration defect. Also indicates the same 'tenant_default disappears and reappears out from under a shared long-lived database' class of risk documented for GH #533 may not be fully closed -- worth checking whether a similar destructive recovery path exists elsewhere, or whether this is purely a cross-workspace stale-binary artifact.
acceptance_criteria: Confirm which of the two candidate mechanisms (stale cross-workspace binary vs. a recurrence of the GH #533 destructive-recovery class) actually caused the 2026-08-08 08:19:53 UTC reprovisioning of bpm_test's tenant_default
If a destructive recovery path is found: remove it per the GH #533 precedent (docs/anti-patterns.md 'Destructive recovery fallbacks (ISS-0209 / GH-533)' entry)

If it is a stale cross-workspace binary: document the risk in docs/anti-patterns.md (a shared long-lived database can be silently reset to a stale schema state by any workspace running an out-of-date migrate binary) and consider whether the shared bpm_test container should be workspace-scoped instead of shared, matching the r-co-2 port-band/compose-project isolation already used for bpm_dev

Re-run GBL-134/GBL-135/GBL-136 (or an equivalent one-off cleanup) against bpm_test once the root cause is fixed, so the 18 tables are dropped again and python3 tools/lint_dual_schema_table_names.py returns exit 0 against bpm_test
Confirm workspace r-co-2's bpm_dev remains unaffected (already confirmed clean at time of filing)
evidence_file: Confirmed via docker exec psql against r-co-2-db_test-1 (2026-08-08, during WF03-GH573-20260808): schema_migrations GROUP BY schema_name shows tenant_default's 75 rows clustered in a 2.5-second window (08:19:53.236205-08:19:55.782928 UTC) versus public's rows spanning 2026-08-06 07:08:54 to 2026-08-08 07:15:57 UTC. python3 tools/lint_dual_schema_table_names.py run against BPM_TEST_DB_URL=postgres://bpm:bpm@localhost:5453/bpm_test returned exit 1 with the 18 names listed above; the same linter run against BPM_TEST_DB_URL=postgres://bpm:bpm@localhost:5452/bpm_dev (workspace r-co-2's own dev DB) returned exit 0, 0 duplicates -- isolating the defect to the shared bpm_test container specifically.
notes: Discovered incidentally while running the mandatory validation suite (zig build, lint_dual_schema_table_names.py, test-env-verify) for ISS-0620/GH-573's forward-fix migration (GBL-137). Not caused by GBL-137 or by ISS-0620's fix -- the 4 tables ISS-0620 concerns (artifact_activation_groups, entity_definitions, entity_record_latest, entity_type_instances) are correctly excluded from this linter's findings (they are now in the ALLOW_LIST as a known, documented, temporary duplicate pending a separate future cleanup migration -- see tools/lint_dual_schema_table_names.py). This is a pre-existing condition in the shared bpm_test database, present before this run started, that this run's own validation surfaced. Per the incidental-discovery protocol (docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md, CLAUDE.md 'No Issue Left Local-Only'), filed as its own issue and forwarded to the global queue rather than fixed on this run's branch.
